# Ship shape needs to point in the direction of travel

## Problem statement

Give the player ship a forward cue: the Asteroids hull's rear edge becomes
concave so the silhouette points along the direction of travel. Scope is the
Asteroids scheme only — the four-directional scheme keeps its invariant
hexagon.

## Users

- **Players** — need an immediate read on which way the ship is facing at all
  times, especially while turning and thrusting in the Asteroids scheme.
- **AI agents / developers** — need a deterministic, geometry-based change that
  keeps `shipSize` semantics, config wiring, physics, and engine-port layout
  intact so existing behaviour and tests carry over.

### Example user stories

- As a **player**, I want the hull silhouette to show a forward direction, so I
  can tell at a glance which way the ship will travel when I thrust.
- As a **player**, I want the cue to stay subtle and consistent with the neon
  geometric palette, so it reads as a ship, not a cartoon arrow.
- As a **developer**, I want the four-directional scheme's invariant hexagon
  untouched, so that scheme's cardinal engine ports and directionless look are
  preserved.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Concave rear edge (Asteroids only):** In the `asteroids` control
  scheme the player hull keeps the hexagon form but its **rear edge** (the side
  opposite the nose, -x in the ship's local frame) is **concave** — a shallow
  inward notch — so the silhouette has a clear forward direction that aligns
  with the ship's facing. The `fourDirectional` scheme keeps the current
  invariant regular hexagon (no notch).
- [ ] **AC2 — Facing alignment & rotation:** The forward cue points along the
  ship's facing: the whole hull (body + concave rear + engine ports) continues
  to rotate with the Graphics object in the Asteroids scheme, so the ship
  visibly points in the direction of travel while turning and thrusting.
  Stationary behaviour holds the **most recent heading** (no snap to a default).
- [ ] **AC3 — Geometry & physics preserved:** The hull's bounding
  circumradius still equals `shipSize / 2` (the notch is an inward cut that must
  not expand the bounding circle); engine port positions (main rear,
  forward-side, nose retro-thruster) stay in the same local frame; no changes to
  `utils/movementModel.ts` physics, input mapping, or firing logic.
- [ ] **AC4 — Config wiring preserved:** Rendering remains driven by
  `ShipConfig` (`shipColor`, `shipSize`, thrust-flame colours/lengths) and works
  with live `setConfig` and the gym sliders. No new config keys.
- [ ] **AC5 — Tests:** Existing four-directional hull tests (6-edge invariant
  hexagon, ports, flames) remain green and unchanged in intent; a new Asteroids
  hull test asserts the concave rear (e.g. an extra interior vertex on the -x
  side / non-straight rear edge) and that the Asteroids silhouette is **not**
  rotationally invariant. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
- [ ] **AC6 — Documentation:** `docs/Game Design Document.md` §7.2 player-hull
  description is amended to describe the Asteroids concave-rear hull (and the
  divergence from the four-directional invariant hexagon); code comments in
  `src/entities/Player.ts` are updated to match.

## Constraints

- Follow GDD §7.2 visual style: geometric/angular silhouettes, neon outline
  (lineStyle 2, `shipColor`, alpha 1), **no fill**; the concave cue must stay
  within the geometric palette (not an organic/curvy shape).
- This deliberately reverses part of the earlier direction-neutral decision
  (AH-0MTBOIIF6004GPY8 / AH-0MTAF76Q1008BLBE): the reversal is scoped to the
  **Asteroids** scheme only; the four-directional scheme keeps the invariant
  hexagon. The GDD must document this scheme divergence.
- `shipSize` keeps its existing meaning (half-size / circumradius used by
  physics-adjacent callers); no physics or input changes.
- Change lives once in the shared `src/entities/Player.ts` so game and gyms
  cannot diverge (gym↔game parity — the player entity is instantiated by
  `PlayScene` and every gym).

## Existing state

- `src/entities/Player.ts` `_redraw()` draws a regular hexagon (flat
  top/bottom, vertices at angles 0°/60°/…/300°, circumradius `shipSize / 2`,
  stroke-only neon) for **both** schemes; the entire Graphics object rotates by
  the facing angle in the Asteroids scheme (`setRotation(facing)`), so the
  hexagon looks identical before and after rotation — no forward cue.
- Engine ports: `FOUR_DIR_ENGINES` (top/bottom/left/right cardinals, size 1)
  and `ASTEROIDS_ENGINES` (main rear at -x, two 70% forward-side at +x, nose
  retro-thruster at +x) drawn as quarter-circle arcs on the hull.
- Tests in `src/entities/Player.test.ts` assert the invariant hexagon
  (6 edge segments, all vertices on the circumradius circle) using the
  four-directional config; gear that keeps asserting the invariant shape is
  shared with the Asteroids-path body test.
- Default `controlScheme` is now `asteroids` (`src/core/configDefaults.ts`).

## Desired change

- In `_redraw()`, when the active scheme is `asteroids`, draw the hull as the
  regular hexagon **with a concave rear edge**: replace the straight -x edge
  (between the two rear vertices) with a shallow inward V-notch (one
  additional interior vertex along the -x side), keeping all other vertices on
  the circumradius circle. When the scheme is `fourDirectional`, draw the
  current invariant hexagon unchanged.
- No change to flames, ports, config, physics, or input. The cue is cosmetic
  but must be structural (deterministic vertex geometry) so it is verifiable in
  tests and identical across game/gyms.

## Key Files

- `src/entities/Player.ts` — `_redraw()` hull geometry: scheme-conditional concave rear edge; update header/comment docs.
- `src/entities/Player.test.ts` — new Asteroids hull test (concave rear / not rotationally invariant); keep existing four-directional hexagon tests intact.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §7.2 player-hull description amended for the Asteroids concave-rear hull and the four-directional divergence.

## Related work

- AH-0MTBOIIF6004GPY8 — *Direction-neutral hexagon body shape* (completed): the design being partially reversed for the Asteroids scheme; hexagon geometry and `shipSize` semantics originate here.
- AH-0MTAF76Q1008BLBE — *Direction-neutral ship shape: circle with engines at top, bottom, and each side* (completed): origin of the neutral-hull rationale and four cardinal engine ports.
- AH-0MTBOMP93002AC25 — *Player entity tests: body shape, engine ports, per-engine flames* (completed): tests pinning the invariant hexagon; must stay green in four-directional form.
- AH-0MTF0EFNZ000RPVD — *Alternative player control* (completed): the Asteroids/four-directional schemes and facing rotation.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §7.2 (player hull) and §2.2/§2.3 (Asteroids facing, reverse thruster, auto-fire heading).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Rendering is hard to assert in tests** (Phaser `Graphics`): mitigated by asserting deterministic vertex geometry (segment count, an interior notch vertex on the -x side) rather than pixels.
- **GDD reversal risk:** reintroducing a direction cue could re-raise the heading ambiguity the neutral hull solved; mitigated by scoping to the Asteroids scheme (which has a real facing) and documenting the scheme divergence in the GDD.
- **Notch depth ambiguity:** "subtle" is not numerically pinned. Assumption: a shallow notch (interior vertex whose distance inward from the straight rear edge is small, e.g. ≤ ~20% of the circumradius, exact value at implementation/discretion) — flag if a specific depth is wanted.
- **Assumption:** the concave notch is the only change in this item — no pointed nose, chevron/arrow redesign, new engine ports, or rotation of the four-directional hull.
- **Scope-creep guard:** pointing the four-directional hull at the velocity heading, a full arrow/chevron redesign, per-scheme config keys, or animated direction cues are **not** in scope — record as new work items if desired.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MTAF76Q1008BLBE** – Direction-neutral ship shape: circle with engines at top, bottom, and each side (completed)
- **AH-0MTECNKPC00954HH** – Test: Per-scene — player/combat assertions + regression (completed)
- **AH-0MUUM1167006CXAK** – EffectsRegistry: Implement hybrid magnet logic (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: clear, currently, direction, edge, forward (+9 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: clear, currently, direction, edge, forward (+9 more)
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: clear, direction, edge, forward, make (+7 more)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Scheme scope:** "Which control scheme(s) get the directional hull?" — **Answer (user):** "(a) Asteroids only" — the default Asteroids scheme gets the directional hull; the four-directional scheme keeps the invariant neutral hexagon (its cardinal engine ports stay cardinal). Source: interactive reply, `/intake` session 2026-10-14.
- **Q2 — Silhouette:** "What silhouette exactly?" — **Answer (user):** "(b) Keep the hexagon outline but make only the rear edge concave (subtle cue)." Source: interactive reply, `/intake` session 2026-10-14. (Classic arrowhead (a) explicitly declined; cue must remain subtle.)
- **Q3 — Stationary nose direction:** "Which way does the nose point when stationary?" — **Answer (user):** "(a) Keep the last heading" — consistent with auto-fire's most-recent-heading fallback and the Asteroids facing. Source: interactive reply, `/intake` session 2026-10-14.

# Periodically validate the human experience against the intended experience

**Priority:** medium · **Issue type:** feature · **Discovered from:** AH-0MV1DLUZ8009OCJW

## Problem statement

Balancing is currently a manual, point-in-time activity. We need a repeatable
way to check that the **human experience** of the game still matches the
**intended experience** (the designed difficulty curve, pacing, progression and
reward cadence), and to detect drift as content and tuning change. This item
builds a periodic validation that compares human-play balance statistics
against explicit intended-experience targets and reports deviations.

## Dependencies

- **Depends on Automated Balancing** (AH-0MV1DLUZ8009OCJW) — provides the bot
  balance statistics and the shared statistics schema.
- **Depends on human-game balance statistics collection** — provides the human
  balance statistics (the dev-mode human recording item).

## User story

- **As a game designer / producer**, I want a periodic report that compares the
  measured human experience (from human play statistics) against the intended
  experience targets, so I can see whether the game still plays as designed and
  where it has drifted.

## Scope

- Define the *intended experience* as explicit, versioned, machine-checkable
  targets (e.g. survival-time band, minerals-per-minute band, upgrades per run,
  wave-reached distribution).
- A periodic run (scheduled or on demand) that compares human statistics
  against those targets and emits a pass/fail + drift report.
- Consume the statistics schema shared with AH-0MV1DLUZ8009OCJW so bot and human
  measurements are compared on the same basis.

## Acceptance criteria (provisional — to be refined at intake)

1. Intended-experience targets are recorded in a versioned, testable form.
2. A periodic validation compares human statistics against the targets and
   reports pass/fail with the magnitude of any drift.
3. The validation is reproducible and covered by tests.
4. Documentation updated; full project test suite passes.

## Related work

- **Automated Balancing** (AH-0MV1DLUZ8009OCJW)
- Human-player balance statistics collection item (dev mode only)
- `docs/EVALUATION.md`, `docs/Game Design Document.md`
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MV1DLUZ8009OCJW** – Automated Balancing (completed)
- **AH-0MV7WVEWL005XEMN** – Collect balance statistics from human player games (dev mode only) (open)
- **AH-0MV8ISO4O002HHDT** – Shared human balance-statistics helper (blocked)

### Repository file matches

- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: activity, balance, band, bot, builds (+80 more)

# Distributed versions of the game do not use the correct Bot definitions

**Priority:** critical · **Issue type:** bug · **Stage:** intake

## Problem statement

Bot-tuning definitions live **only** in `window.localStorage` (key
`ai-hell-bot-tuning`, written by `src/core/botTuningStore.ts`), and the
shipped **Watch Demo** / attract mode (`PlayScene` demo mode) reads that store
when a demo starts. `localStorage` is per-browser, per-origin and per-machine —
it is not part of the repository or of a build. When the code is checked out on
another machine, or served from a distributed build (e.g. the GitHub Pages
alpha), a fresh browser has no saved state and every demo silently falls back
to the built-in `Default` config instead of the tuned Bot definitions the
developer has in their build environment. The enemy/ship/difficulty CSVs do
ship with the build (bundled via `?raw` in `src/core/bundledConfig.ts`); bot
tuning has no equivalent, which is why only bot behaviour is affected.

**Goal:** a Git-tracked bot-tuning configuration is bundled into every build as
the baseline, so distributed builds and fresh machines fly the correct Bot
definitions, while a local user's saved `localStorage` selection still wins
locally.

## Users

- **Developer / designer of the demo bot:** tunes named configurations in the
  Bot Tuning gym, and expects every build of the game — including one checked
  out or served on another machine — to fly those definitions rather than the
  generic factory defaults.
- **Producer / release reviewer:** runs demos and records gameplay video
  (`npm run capture`, `npm run record -- --bot`) from any checkout and expects
  the footage to show the tuned bot, not a default fallback.

Example user stories:

- *As a developer tuning the demo bot, I want the tuned configuration committed
  to the repo so that a fresh checkout, build and demo run plays my tuning
  without re-exporting anything.*
- *As a producer, I want the GitHub Pages alpha to show the correct bot
  behaviour so release footage and preview builds match the tuned design.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1 — Bundled baseline ships and is used.** A Git-tracked bot-tuning
   configuration file (the exact exported store shape `{ version, current,
   configs }`) is committed and bundled into dev and production builds; in a
   browser with no (or corrupt/missing) `localStorage` state,
   `loadBotTuningState()` returns the bundled configuration set and the shipped
   demo (`PlayScene` demo mode) flies it.
2. **AC2 — Local overrides are preserved.** When `localStorage` holds a saved
   state, the currently-selected local configuration wins locally — precedence
   is `localStorage` → bundled baseline, mirroring the CSV config pattern; a
   fresh browser shows the bundled baseline, not factory defaults.
3. **AC3 — Corrupt-safe, unchanged fallback behaviour.** Missing/invalid
   `localStorage` (and an unreadable/invalid bundled file) never crashes or
   degrades demo behaviour; the store remains versioned and corrupt-safe.
4. **AC4 — Refresh workflow round-trips.** The bundled file is byte-equivalent
   to the Bot Tuning gym's **Export** output (via
   `serialiseBotTuningState()`), so *tune → Export → commit → build → fresh
   browser* reproduces the tuned demo; the workflow is documented.
5. **AC5 — Recording tools see the baseline.** `npm run capture` (demo path)
   and `npm run record -- --bot` launched without `--bot-config` in a fresh
   Chromium now record the bundled baseline (previously factory defaults);
   passing `--bot-config` still overrides for a specific clip.
6. **AC6 — Testing/validation.** Unit and integration tests cover the fallback
   and precedence; `npm run typecheck` and `npm run build` pass; the gym↔game
   duplicate-body parity guard stays green.
7. **AC7 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect
   the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs
   site entries (`docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`,
   `docs/dev/recording-and-replay.md`, `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` §12).
8. **AC8 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- No changes to bot *decision* code — only which tunables construct the
  brain/governor (consistent with AH-0MV6MFDYG001E6PL non-goals).
- The store's persistence model stays `localStorage`; the bundled file is a
  baseline fallback, not a new write path.
- The shipped file must be **Git-tracked** (never git-ignored).
- Normal (human) Play Game sessions stay untouched — the bot seam remains
  inert outside demo mode.
- No schema/version bump is expected (`BOT_TUNING_SCHEMA_VERSION = 1` shape is
  reused).

## Existing state

- `src/core/botTuningStore.ts` — `createDefaultState()` seeds only the built-in
  `Default` config; `parseState()` already validates the exact exported
  `{ version, current, configs }` shape and is corruption-safe, so a bundled
  JSON blob can reuse it.
- `src/core/bundledConfig.ts` — the established bundling point for Git-tracked
  design data (`?raw` CSV imports consumed by production/static builds).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — demo mode already calls
  `getCurrentBotTuningConfig()` on start and rebuilds the brain/governor
  (AH-0MV6MFDYG001E6PL); no change needed there.
- `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` / `scripts/record-session.mjs` — launch a
  fresh Chromium; inject `--bot-config` only when the flag is passed.
- Docs: `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` (§ Bot-tuning configuration),
  `docs/dev/recording-and-replay.md`, `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` (§12).

## Desired change

1. **Add the shipped baseline.** Commit a new `src/data/bot-tuning.json` holding
   the exported store state (produced via the gym's **Export** button /
   `serialiseBotTuningState()` from the developer's build environment) and
   export it from `src/core/bundledConfig.ts` (JSON import or a `?raw` parse,
   matching how the CSVs bundle).
2. **Make it the fallback.** In `src/core/botTuningStore.ts`,
   `createDefaultState()` / `parseState()` no longer default to the lone
   factory `Default` when storage is empty; instead the bundled file is parsed
   through the existing `parseState()` validation (which already falls back
   safely on malformed input) so a fresh browser seeds the bundled
   configurations — keeping a `Default`-named entry that carries the shipped
   values so the gym selector and config-name reporting are unchanged.
   Precedence stays `localStorage` → bundled baseline.
3. **Docs.** Document the baseline, the precedence rule, and the refresh
   workflow (tune → Export → overwrite `src/data/bot-tuning.json` → commit).
4. **Tests.** Add store tests (no storage / corrupt storage / invalid bundled
   file → bundled baseline; saved storage wins), a demo-mode test asserting the
   demo flies the bundled baseline in a fresh profile, and keep capture-script
   tests green.

## Key Files

- `src/data/bot-tuning.json` — **new**, Git-tracked baseline (exported store
  shape).
- `src/core/bundledConfig.ts` — export the bundled bot-tuning baseline.
- `src/core/botTuningStore.ts` — seed from the bundled baseline when storage is
  empty/invalid.
- `src/core/botTuningStore.test.ts` — new baseline/precedence cases.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` / demo-mode integration test — verify the fresh
  profile demo flies the bundled baseline.
- `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` — unchanged code; verify fresh-browser capture
  uses the baseline (test/doc only).
- Docs: `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`, `docs/dev/recording-and-replay.md`,
  `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md`.

## Related work

- `Watch Demo and video recording should fly the saved bot-tuning configuration (AH-0MV6MFDYG001E6PL)` —
  completed; introduced the localStorage store read by demo mode and the
  `--bot-config` flow. This bug is the distribution gap that feature left open.
- `Gym scene for AI bot tuning (AH-0MV4D7LAD009XYR0)` — completed; the tuning
  gym + store.
- `Config store: in-memory registry, boot load, dev write (AH-0MUE2MGZM0016U3L)` /
  `Create a CSV file to maintain enemy configurations (AH-0MTZWZ9TE009CVUA)` —
  completed; the CSV bundling pattern this fix mirrors.
- Duplicate check performed — no overlapping item found.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** "the correct Bot definitions" are the Bot Tuning gym's named
  configurations (confirmed with the operator).
- **Assumption:** the shipped baseline should apply identically in dev and
  production/distributed builds, with local `localStorage` overriding locally
  (confirmed with the operator).
- **Risk — stale baseline:** the committed file can drift from current tuning.
  *Mitigation:* document the refresh workflow; keep the file as the single
  source of the shipped baseline (like the CSVs).
- **Risk — surprising local overrides:** a user who previously saved the old
  `Default` values in `localStorage` keeps them locally. *Mitigation:* expected
  and consistent with the CSV/localStorage precedence; documented.
- **Scope creep — automatic sync** of local gym edits back to the repo (a
  dev-mode write path analogous to the CSV plugin) is **out of scope** here and
  should be recorded as a separate work item if wanted.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "What are the 'Bot definitions' that should travel?" — Answer (producer,
  interactive): "A — the Bot Tuning gym's named configurations
  (`ai-hell-bot-tuning`) that Watch Demo / attract mode flies."
  Source: interactive reply. Research: `src/core/botTuningStore.ts` is the only
  persistence; demo mode in `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` (`_applyBotTuning`)
  reads it; CSVs ship via `src/core/bundledConfig.ts`.
- Q: "How should the tuned bot definition reach a distributed build?" —
  Answer (producer, interactive): "A — commit a Git-tracked bot-tuning config
  file, bundled into the build like the CSVs (baseline), with localStorage
  still able to override locally." Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "On a fresh machine/browser, which should win?" — Answer (producer,
  interactive): "A — the shipped baseline config is the effective default; a
  user's local localStorage selection overrides it locally (mirrors the CSV
  pattern)." Source: interactive reply.


## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MV81YJQP008L9CQ** – Balance statistics schema and pure aggregation (completed)
- **AH-0MV81YY2T0069W19** – Versioned balance report and CLI batch flags (completed)
- **AH-0MV8QT7CB0060A7A** – Extend the headless arena to simulate the full shipped campaign (waves, levels, upgrades) (open)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: another, bot, build, code, correct (+11 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: another, bot, build, code, correct (+10 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: another, bot, build, code, correct (+10 more)

data.comment: RCA (intake): bot-tuning definitions live only in window.localStorage ('ai-hell-bot-tuning', src/core/botTuningStore.ts) and PlayScene demo mode reads that store when a demo starts. localStorage is per-browser/per-origin/per-machine and is not part of the repo or build, so a checkout on another machine (fresh browser or a distributed/GitHub Pages build) always falls back to the built-in Default config — never the tuned 'Bot definitions'. Unlike the enemy/ship/difficulty CSVs (bundled via ?raw in src/core/bundledConfig.ts), no bot config ships with the build. Interview decisions: (1) scope = Bot Tuning gym named configurations; (2) fix = commit a Git-tracked bot-tuning config bundled into the build as the baseline (like the CSVs), localStorage overrides locally; (3) shipped baseline is the effective default for a fresh browser, local localStorage selection wins locally. Related: AH-0MV6MFDYG001E6PL (Watch Demo flies saved bot-tuning config) — completed feature that introduced this store read.
